## The sandbox

A private repository's installs and checks run on **Cloudflare Containers**: one Durable Object drives one container, and each side of a run gets its own. A public repository's, and every dry run's, run on [Token Factory Sandboxes](/docs/build/token-factory-sandboxes), a microVM per command, with no network interface during the checks.

On Cloudflare Containers:

| Rule | How |
|---|---|
| No direct internet | Containers start with `enableInternet: false`. All HTTP and HTTPS goes through Teire's egress handler |
| Install: registries only | `GET` and `HEAD` over HTTPS to 25 hosts: npm and Yarn, PyPI, Maven Central and Google's mirror, Gradle, the Go proxy, crates.io and the Rust toolchain, RubyGems, Adoptium, and GitHub with its release assets |
| Checks: nothing | Every request is answered `403` and recorded with its host, method and path. Denied hosts appear in the PR |
| No secrets inside | The repository arrives as a tarball the egress handler fetches **outside** the container, adding the GitHub token itself. The token is dropped after the fetch. Model keys never enter |
| No install scripts | npm, pnpm, Yarn v1 and Bun install with `--ignore-scripts`, Yarn Berry with `--mode=skip-build` |
| One token per sandbox | Each sandbox needs its own signed token (HMAC-SHA256). The worker signs it for 15 minutes; the service refuses anything valid for over 2 hours |
| Bounded | Each job has a 60-minute ceiling, each command's output is capped, and an idle container stops after 15 minutes |
| Nothing left behind | Tearing a sandbox down deletes its container and all its stored state |

The worker never runs your repository's code. It reads packages with static tools: TypeScript declarations, griffe, apidiff, Prism, japicmp on jars, and ast-grep. Tarballs are integrity-checked and unpacked by Teire's own extractor, which refuses links and `..` paths.

## The dependency updater

Manifest and lockfile changes are moving to dependabot-core's updater ([How Teire updates dependency files](/docs/build/dependency-files)). It runs on Teire's own server, not in the verification sandbox:

- in a separate Docker daemon whose containers run under gVisor;
- on a network with no route out, behind Dependabot's proxy and a host firewall that blocks Teire's apps, its database, cloud metadata and every host port;
- with a token that can only read the one repository, held by the proxy, never by the updater;
- with images pinned by digest, whose build attestations are checked before use;
- one job at a time.

The [threat model](https://github.com/teire-dev/teire/blob/main/apps/resolver/THREAT-MODEL.md) lists each control and the probe that proves it.

## The agent

The model is handed file contents, documentation, check output and provider pages **as data, never as instructions**. Code limits what it can do:

- It edits only the files the change reaches and the files your check output names.
- It never edits manifests, lockfiles, `tsconfig`, build config, CI, `.env` files or credentials.
- It can't read `.env*`, `.git/`, `node_modules/` or key files.
- It must not delete, skip or weaken tests, or add new casts, `any` or type-ignore comments. The review checks the final diff for exactly these.

## Provider data

A provider's change is acted on only when its quote is found word for word in the page Teire fetched from the provider's own domain. See [the quote gate](/docs/ecosystems/providers#the-quote-gate). Items whose quote fails are dropped; records that fail the final checks are kept as unconfirmed and never applied.

## On GitHub

| Permission | Access | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Contents | write | Read the code and dependency files; push one branch per fix (`teire/…`). Never the default branch |
| Pull requests | write | Open and update fix PRs, and the Configure Teire onboarding PR |
| Issues | write | Keep the Teire Dashboard issue, open needs-a-human issues, and answer `@teire` commands |
| Checks | write | Publish the Teire check run with an annotation on every line a change reaches |
| Actions | read | Read your CI's logs when it fails on a Teire PR, for one repair attempt |
| Metadata | read | Repository names and default branches; GitHub requires it for every app |
| Email addresses | read | Your account's email when you sign in with GitHub, to name your account; never emailed |

Teire never merges and never pushes to your default branch. Commands and dashboard actions need write access to the repository.

## Where your code goes

- **Models.** Only NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory reads code.
- **Search.** Tavily receives search queries that name a provider, such as "Groq API deprecations…", never code.
- **Storage.** A scan downloads the repository at one commit and deletes it when the scan ends. Teire keeps the findings (file, line and the matching line), the diffs it proposes, run logs, receipts, and the tail of each sandbox command's output.
